concepts.title: Oxidation, Reduction and Redox Reactions
concepts.definition: A redox reaction couples oxidation, the loss of electrons or gain of oxygen, with reduction, the gain of electrons or loss of hydrogen, so that one species is oxidised and another reduced in the same reaction, and the species supplying electrons is the reducing agent while the one accepting them is the oxidising agent.
concepts.key_idea: Oxidation number increases during oxidation and decreases during reduction, giving a bookkeeping method that applies even to covalent compounds.

concepts.title: Assigning Oxidation Number by the Sum Rule
concepts.definition: Oxidation number is assigned by rules of ion charge and electronegativity, and in any neutral molecule the sum of oxidation numbers of all atoms is zero while in a polyatomic ion it equals the charge of the ion, letting the unknown oxidation number be solved from the known ones.
concepts.key_idea: Fluorine always shows -1, oxygen usually -2 and hydrogen +1 in compounds, providing the fixed values for the sum rule.

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the sum of known oxidation numbers from the total charge and divide by the number of unknown atoms

concepts.title: Balancing Redox Reactions: Oxidation Number and Half Reaction Methods
concepts.definition: Redox equations are balanced either by the oxidation number method, equalising total increase and decrease in oxidation numbers, or by the ion electron half reaction method, where oxidation and reduction half reactions are balanced separately for atoms, charge, oxygen with water and hydrogen with hydrogen ion, then added.
concepts.key_idea: Redox reactions are classified into combination, decomposition, displacement and disproportionation types, the last being a reaction in which the same element is both oxidised and reduced.

solution_steps.explain: Balance elements, then oxygen with water, hydrogen with hydrogen ion, and charge with electrons.

concepts.title: Redox Reactions in Daily Life and Electrode Processes
concepts.definition: Redox reactions underlie electrochemical cells where oxidation occurs at the anode and reduction at the cathode, batteries and fuel cells, corrosion of metals, and electrolysis, connecting chemistry to energy technology and metallurgy.
concepts.key_idea: In a galvanic cell the spontaneous redox reaction generates current, and electrode potential measures the tendency of an electrode to lose or gain electrons.
